blocks.text: Show the keyboard shortcuts list in Slack on Mac

Start with the desktop app. Slack's Help Center gives one instruction for this. Press ⌘ / (Command and slash) from Slack on your desktop, and the list appears in a panel on the right side of the screen. That is the whole answer for most people. The rest of this page covers the steps in detail, the Mac keys worth learning next, and what to do when the list does not open.
Why ⌘ / and not a menu item

You might expect a Keyboard Shortcuts item in the menu bar. Slack's documentation does not describe one. The Help Center documents a key combination, not a menu path, so the shortcut is the reliable route. Spend your time on the keys, not on hunting through menus.

The key itself deserves a second look. Slack's main keyboard shortcuts article has garbled text that seems to show ⌘ , for the list. Two other Slack help pages say ⌘ /. That is the instruction to follow.

blocks.title: Which key to press
blocks.text: Use ⌘ /. The ⌘ , shortcut opens preferences in the desktop app. The main article's garbled text looks like ⌘ , for the list, but the two other Slack pages both say ⌘ /.
Mac keys to learn after the list

Once you know where the list lives, a few keys do most of the daily work. Slack's Mac table lists them. Some work only in the desktop app, which matters if you move between the app and a browser tab. The table below shows each key and where Slack says it works.

blocks.text: Start with ⌘ J if you come back to Slack after a meeting. It jumps to your first unread message, and Slack marks it desktop only. Add ⌘ G for search next, because it saves a trip to the search box.
Turn on Full Keyboard Access for Tab then M

Tab then M opens the Message Actions menu on a Mac. Slack's help article says it works only when Full Keyboard Access is on. Full Keyboard Access is a macOS setting, not a key combination, so you cannot switch it on from inside Slack.
Open System Settings and search for Full Keyboard Access. Turn it on. Apple changes pane names between macOS releases, so search for the name rather than following a fixed route.
Be aware that this setting changes how Tab works in other apps too. Tab moves focus through more controls, not just text fields. If that gets in your way, turn it off again.
When the shortcuts list does not open

Most failures come from three causes. The wrong app is in front, a browser tab has focus instead of the desktop app, or another app takes ⌘ / before Slack sees it. Check them in that order. Each check takes only a few seconds.

items: Slack is not the active app, so the keys go somewhere else.
A browser tab has focus instead of the desktop app.
Another app or keyboard utility uses ⌘ / first.

blocks.text: Using the list in the web app or on Windows

Slack's instruction applies to the desktop app on Mac. The Help Center names Ctrl / for Windows and Linux, so the key changes on those systems. The Slack pages checked for this page do not confirm ⌘ / in a browser tab, so do not assume it works there.

Two shortcuts are documented as desktop only. They are ⌘ J for the first unread message and ⌘ , for preferences. If you rely on either one, stay in the desktop app. The browser may behave differently.
Move between sections with the keyboard

Slack's navigation article covers moving between sections. In the desktop app, F6 and Shift F6 move between sections, and ⌘ → and ⌘ ← do the same job. In a browser, the Mac keys are ⌘ F6 and ⌘ ⇧ F6. Use the desktop keys inside the app and the browser keys only in a tab.
Why a shortcut list saves real time

Switching between tools has a cost. A Lokalise vendor survey of 1,000 US knowledge workers across 11 industries reports an average of 33 tab, app, or platform switches per day. The same survey puts the time lost to tool fatigue at about 51 minutes per week. Lokalise sells localization software, so treat those figures as directional.
A secondary source citing a 2005 CHI paper says workers are interrupted every 6 to 12 minutes. The original paper was not checked for this page, so verify it before you quote it.
A shortcut will not stop interruptions. It does remove the detour to the mouse and the hunt through menus. That detour is the part you control.
Mistakes people make with Slack shortcuts

items: Pressing ⌘ , and expecting the list. In the desktop app, that key opens preferences.
Looking for a setting to remap keys. Slack says custom keyboard shortcuts are not possible.
Trusting ⌘ K without checking it. The Navigate article lists it for opening a channel or DM, but the main Mac table leaves it out.
Using a browser tab and wondering why the list is missing. Slack documents the instruction for the desktop app.
Assuming Tab then M works by default. It needs Full Keyboard Access in macOS.

blocks.text: Practice the list without risk
Reading the list once does not make the keys stick. Practice in a quiet place where a mistake costs nothing. A draft message or an empty channel works well for this.

items: Open the Slack desktop app and press ⌘ / once.
Read the panel for about one minute without touching anything else.
Pick three keys you will use every day, such as ⌘ J, ⌘ G and ⌘ F.
Press each key once and note whether it did what the panel says.

blocks.text: Repeat the routine for a few days. The keys you use most will start to feel automatic, and the panel becomes a backup instead of a crutch.
Where Lazur fits in

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

For this task, that means two useful things. If the shortcuts panel is open, you can ask where it is and Lazur points at it. If you forget which key opens a menu, ask, and Lazur points at that menu on screen. Lazur does not press ⌘ / for you, and it does not change Slack's settings.

Lazur is not a plugin for any app, Slack included. It works across apps on the Mac. It looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer, and they are not stored.
Next steps after you open the list

If unread messages slow you down, read [how to view unread messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/view-all-unread-messages-in-slack). For the ⌘ , shortcut and where preferences live, see [how to open preferences in Slack on Mac](/how-to/open-preferences-in-slack). Search has its own page, [how to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack), which covers ⌘ G in context.

Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. You can [download it here](/download), and current plans are on [the pricing page](/pricing). Check the pricing page before you decide, because plan details can change.

faq.question: Is there a menu item for keyboard shortcuts in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Slack's help pages give the ⌘ / shortcut and do not describe a menu path. Searching the menu bar for a shortcuts item costs time. Press the key combination instead.

faq.question: Why doesn't ⌘ , show the shortcuts list?
faq.answer: ⌘ , opens preferences in the Slack desktop app. One Slack article has garbled text that seems to show it for the list, but two other Slack help pages say ⌘ /. Use ⌘ /.

faq.question: Can I change the shortcut to something easier to remember?
faq.answer: No. Slack's keyboard shortcuts article says it is not currently possible to set custom keyboard shortcuts. Learn the built-in keys and keep the panel as your reference.

faq.question: Does ⌘ / work in the Slack web app?
faq.answer: Slack documents ⌘ / for the desktop app. The pages checked for this page do not confirm it in a browser. Open the desktop app for this shortcut.

faq.question: Which Slack version do these steps match?
faq.answer: No Slack help article ties these steps to a version. The latest Mac release this page could confirm is 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026, according to Slack's release notes.

faq.question: Does Lazur press ⌘ / for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. Hold Option and Command, ask where the list is, and Lazur points at it on screen while the panel is open.

faq.question: Is Lazur built into Slack?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that works across apps. It is not a plugin for any app, Slack included, and it does not operate Slack for you.

steps.name: Open the Slack desktop app
steps.text: Open Slack from the Dock or the Applications folder. Slack documents this shortcut for the desktop app. The pages checked for this page do not confirm it in a browser tab, so use the app for these steps.
steps.tip: A Slack window open in Chrome or Safari is not the desktop app. Check the app name in the Dock.

steps.name: Make Slack the active app
steps.text: Click once inside the Slack window. Keyboard shortcuts go to whichever app is in front. If another app is active, ⌘ / goes there, and nothing happens in Slack.

steps.name: Press ⌘ / to open the list
steps.text: Hold Command, tap the slash key, then let go of both keys. Slack's instruction names the slash character, so use the key that types /. On a US keyboard, that key sits next to the right Shift key.
steps.tip: Do not add Shift. Command, Shift and slash is a different combination, and Slack's table does not list it.

steps.name: Read the panel on the right
steps.text: The full list opens in a panel on the right side of the Slack window. Scroll with two fingers on the trackpad. Keep the main window visible so you can try a shortcut while you read.
steps.tip: Try one shortcut as soon as you read it. Keys stick faster when you use them.

steps.name: Close the panel
steps.text: Close the panel the way you close other side panels in Slack. Pressing ⌘ / again may also work, but Slack's help pages do not say it toggles the list. Test it before you rely on it.

steps.name: Check the panel against your version
steps.text: Slack's 2026 Mac release notes do not mention keyboard shortcuts, so the panel itself is the best reference. The latest release this page could confirm is 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026. If your copy is newer, trust the panel over this page.
steps.tip: Keep the panel open for a minute, then close it. Repeat until the keys feel automatic.

troubleshooting.fix: Click the Slack window once to make it active. Check that you are in the desktop app, not a browser tab. If it still fails, look for another app that uses ⌘ / and close it or change its shortcut.
That key opens preferences in the desktop app, as Slack documents. Close the window and press ⌘ / instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The list is missing in the browser
troubleshooting.fix: Use the desktop app. Slack documents ⌘ / for the desktop app, and the pages checked for this page do not confirm it in a browser tab.

troubleshooting.problem: Tab then M does not open Message Actions
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on Full Keyboard Access in macOS System Settings. Slack's help article says the menu opens only with that setting on.

troubleshooting.problem: The slash key is in a different spot on my keyboard
troubleshooting.fix: Slack names the slash character, not a key position. Find the key that types / on your layout and hold Command with it. Test in a text field first if the layout is new to you.

troubleshooting.problem: A key in the panel does not match what happens
troubleshooting.fix: Slack's shortcuts can change, and the panel is the reference. Trust the panel over an old cheat sheet, and note the key for later.
